clause_i.reason: The generator varies signed pulse speed (-1 or +1) and the initial pulse/receiver phases across instances. An observation-free q using only I_t and task times cannot select the sign- and phase-appropriate pointer_hold action for every history in the grouped active-relay mode.

clause_ii.reason: The five chronological frames in the bounded 500 ms window visibly expose pulse/receiver positions, their motion direction, active stage, phase error, contact, and charge. Given I_t and the fixed profile physics, g can predict the state after Delta=375 ms and choose the optimal keyboard/pointer action.

clause_iii.reason: Common witness inside the pointer_hold control mode: take H_t just after a locked tick with direction=sign(speed), receiver=pulse, contact=false, and charge=7. Choose a generated stage with |speed|=1; receiver/pulse relative drift is 7°/tick. If no new action arrives for 5 ticks (Delta=375 ms), the visible error becomes 35° > the 30° aperture and contact-off ticks reduce charge to 2. At H_t, pointerdown/held pointer contact reaches the aperture on the next tick and supplies the final charge unit; at H_t^Delta the same action is outside the aperture and has strictly lower immediate relay/charge advantage. The stage remains recoverable within its 420-tick limit, so the strict loss is caused by visible phase/charge evolution, not merely a deadline.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The common process is the active relay phase bus: the visible pulse marker rotates every 75 ms, the receiver marker advances under the selected drive, and phase loss visibly drains charge. The same process supplies the recent-frame evidence for delayed action selection and makes the pointer_hold contact opportunity degrade.

pre_run.reason: Source-structural pre-run witness: this profile has exactly one stage. No further outcome-affecting action is needed before the single relay ends, and VERIFY IDENTITY is administrative. At least half is therefore met; no percentage is asserted.
